plan: This is a second-price auction structure (sealed bid acts as exit point in ascending clock, winner pays second-highest bid). In such mechanisms, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit since you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid and pay only that amount, never overpaying relative to your value. With no prior history to adjust for, I'll bid exactly my value of $22.

This auction mechanism functions like a second-price auction: my sealed bid acts as my exit point in the ascending clock, and I'll pay the second-highest bid if I win. In such mechanisms, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $15.

Since the sealed bid acts as my exit point in an ascending clock auction, this mimics a second-price auction mechanism. The dominant strategy in such auctions is to bid my true value, as this ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the market price (other bids) and pay only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying.
